Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA), in force since 1 October 2014
World Trade Organization Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended, and Regulations SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, ss. 83.01 et seq. and s. 462.31; Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2236 et seq. (société en commandite / limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR, c. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of UBO's valid passport or national identity document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Consular or notarial authority in the UBO's jurisdiction of nationality or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing state is a party to the Apostille Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization at a Canadian embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / status for any foreign corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or companies registrar in the general partner's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney / mandate conferring signature authority on the Quebec representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or competent authority in the principal's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds documentation for the LP's initial capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or financial institution of the contributing partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization, then Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified translation into French of the limited partnership agreement and constitutional documents, if not already in French
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified translator recognized by the Quebec professional order of translators
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized translator's certificate; no apostille required for the translation itself

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory identity verification and beneficial-ownership determination under the PCMLTFA before onboarding; screen all natural persons holding at least 25% ownership or control against the UN Consolidated List, Canadian United Nations Act regulations, Special Economic Measures Act, Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists, FINTRAC's politically exposed person (PEP) definitions and indicators, Interpol notices where available, and Quebec provincial law-enforcement records. OFAC SDN screening is additionally applied whenever USD clearing, U.S. payment rails, or U.S. counterparties are used. Enhanced due diligence is required for trusts, shell entities, bearer-share structures, high-risk jurisdictions, or unexplained source of funds.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Quebec Enterprise Registrar — Registraire des entreprises du Québec online portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, the declared enterprise name must be in French. A non-French name or version may be used only where a French version is registered together or a statutory exemption applies, such as a recognized trademark. Non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters, and the name must not mislead as to legal form, partnership character, or the nature and scale of activities.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the registrar issues a written refusal citing the statutory ground. Within 30 days the applicant may file an amended declaration using a corrected name that addresses the refusal, or may submit an administrative review request to the Registraire des entreprises attaching the refusal notice, the enterprise name search results, and any trademark or ministerial consents. A name approval may not be automatically extended; a new name search and reservation filing may be submitted before expiry. If the registrar confirms the refusal, the applicant may appeal to the Court of Quebec under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, or apply for ministerial approval where the issue concerns a restricted or sensitive token. Further recourse is available by judicial review before the Superior Court of Quebec.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for a Quebec limited partnership whose business is principally e-commerce merchandising of designer vinyl collectibles, provided the declared registered office is a physical street address in Quebec, is not a post-office box, can receive mail and service of legal process, and books and records remain accessible. A commercial virtual office, co-working address, or a law/notary office may serve as the principal establishment for registration and service purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 10% likelihood of an unannounced inspection of the registered office within the first 12 months; 20% likelihood for any physical warehouse or production premise used for toy assembly, finishing, or fulfillment, given Health Canada's inspection powers under the Canada Consumer Product Safety Act, S.C. 2010, c. 21, and Revenu Québec's unannounced audit and records-examination powers.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Estimated appeal filing fee and legal review rate

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec (CQLR c CCQ-1991), arts. 2186–2274 (société en commandite / limited partnership); Act respecting the Registraire des entreprises (CQLR c E-12.1), ss. 21–57 (registration, declaration, and legal publicity); Taxation Act (CQLR c I-3), Part II (partnership fiscal transparency)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec / Quebec Enterprise Registrar (online portal: Mon Compte et services en ligne)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration) of a Québec société en commandite
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-in capital; contributions may be in cash, in kind, or services (arts. 2202–2208 CCQ); no statutory escrow account is required; capital withdrawals by limited partners are restricted to preserve creditor protection
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the formation in Quebec of the limited partnership (société en commandite) to be known as [Name] be approved; the General Partner is directed to execute and file the Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and to open the undertaking's statutory register. RESOLVED, that the partnership agreement and the schedule of capital contributions subscribed by the limited partners be adopted and recorded in the capital account ledger. RESOLVED, that the registered office be fixed at [address], Province of Quebec; [Name] is appointed manager with authority to operate bank accounts, engage contractors, and procure licences. RESOLVED, that all registrations with Revenu Québec and the Canada Revenue Agency be completed without delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name search and reservation through the Quebec Enterprise Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Online Distinctive Name Search and Reservation (Mon Compte)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary search on the registrar's public database; submit a Declaration of Reservation of Name identifying a distinctive element followed by 'S.E.C.' or 'L.P.'; the registrar reserves an available name for 90 days. Attest that the general partner authorizes use of the name.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate names (3 alternatives)
Identification and address of the general partner
Attestation of consent to use the proposed name
Business activity description (SCIAN/NAICS 339930)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, revise the distinctive element and refile a new reservation request; no formal appeal lies, but the applicant may submit a written objection and receive a written refusal reason within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of partnership agreement and capital subscription ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private instrument drafted by counsel; no filing with a government registry at this step
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the partnership agreement stipulating the firm name, Quebec registered office, object (manufacture of designer vinyl collectibles), contributions by limited partners, profit-sharing ratio, and management authority of the general partner. Notarization is not mandatory unless real property is contributed. Record subscriptions in a capital account ledger.
required_dossiers: Partnership agreement (société en commandite)
Schedule of committed capital contributions
Capital account ledger
Unanimous consent of partners to initial management appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: No adverse administrative action applies to this private step; any internal disagreement is cured by a supplementary unanimous resolution or an amended agreement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Declaration of Registration (immatriculation) and issuance of Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online submission via Mon Compte
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the déclaration d'immatriculation indicating the form 'société en commandite', full name and domicile of the general partner, Quebec registered office, postal address, business activity (SCIAN 339930 – doll, toy and game manufacturing), and names of authorized managers. Pay the CAD 79 registration fee electronically; the registrar issues the attestation of registration and the NEQ upon approval.
required_dossiers: Completed Declaration of Registration form
Name reservation certificate (or chosen name approval)
Government-issued identification of the general partner
Proof of Quebec registered office address
Declaration of principal establishment (établissement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a query (demande de renseignements) is issued, respond with corrective declarations within 30 days; if the registrar refuses registration, seek rectification under s. 76 of the Act respecting the Registraire des entreprises and, failing that, apply for judicial review before the Cour du Québec within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for Quebec and federal tax accounts (QST, GST/HST, payroll)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec – Mon dossier entreprise; Canada Revenue Agency – Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the issued NEQ, register the limited partnership for Québec Sales Tax (QST), pension/QPIP contributions, and employer health contributions; obtain a federal GST/HST account and CRA payroll account linked to the same business number. Designate the general partner as the responsible representative for tax filings and provide for the allocation of income among partners.
required_dossiers: NEQ attestation of registration
Partnership agreement and capital allocation schedule
Canadian social insurance numbers or business numbers of general partners
Bank account confirmation (or letter of intent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax registration is rejected or held pending, cure by extracting a current attestation from the Registraire and resubmitting; disputes on taxable status may be resolved by written notice of objection to Revenu Québec within 45 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal establishment permit and workplace occupational clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Applicable municipalité locale (e.g., Ville de Montréal arrondissement permits office); Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ); Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the occupancy permit (permis d'établissement) application for the industrial unit together with a fire safety plan, machinery layout, and proof of lease. Obtain RBQ review for structural load and building-code compliance of rotocasting ovens, vent hoods, and spray booths. Register as an employer with CNESST, adopt a workplace prevention program, and schedule a machine-guarding inspection.
required_dossiers: Lease or certificate of right to occupy the industrial premises
Fire safety plan approved by municipal fire prevention service
RBQ building/installation certificate for ventilation and kilns
Machinery floor plan and hazardous-materials inventory
CNESST employer registration and accident prevention program
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the permit is refused, remedy the deficiencies listed in the municipal inspector's report and reapply within 30 days; contest a CNESST stop-work order before the Tribunal administratif du travail within 60 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Canadian banking account and statutory records maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial institution of choice (e.g., National Bank, RBC) – branch or online; Registraire des entreprises du Québec for annual declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Provide the charter documents, NEQ attestation, partnership agreement, and general partner resolution to open a business account; deposit initial partner contributions and maintain a separate capital ledger. Diarize the annual declaration renewal with the Registraire and prepare KYC/AML profile conforming to low-risk standard for designer toy merchandising.
required_dossiers: Attestation of registration from the Registraire
Partnership agreement
General partner resolution appointing signatories
Certified identification of signing officers
AML/KYC self-certification and source-of-funds statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional corporate due diligence, supply a certified copy of the current attestation and a certificate of incumbency; escalate to the bank's business onboarding team if the standard SLA is exceeded.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE) – sector development; municipalité locale – zoning and industrial occupancy permits; no provincial manufacturing license is reserved for vinyl toy rotocasting
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No dedicated provincial manufacturing permit required for designer collectible toys; applicable general instruments are the municipal occupancy/business licence, Revenu Québec establishment registration, and CNESST workplace declaration

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) – Service de l'évaluation environnementale et des établissements industriels
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration tier – not a Category I full EIA project; the activity is subject to voluntary registration under the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment (O.C. 682-2024) and to municipal pre-treatment by-laws for industrial wastewater; a full EIA is not triggered unless production reaches a large industrial threshold or the site is in a sensitive zone.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: BOD5 ≤ 15 mg/L, TSS ≤ 30 mg/L, pH 6.0–9.5 (municipal sewer pre-treatment); VOC emissions from rotocasting ovens and airbrush booths limited to ≤ 500 t/yr in a given permitting cycle, thereafter requiring an attestation of environmental authorization; residual plastic, paints, and solvent wastes must be rendered to a permitted recycler under the Quebec Residual Materials Regulation (RLRQ c Q-2, r. 46).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal fire prevention certificate confirming sprinklers, exits, and storage of combustibles; RBQ structural load clearance for kilns and injection presses; CNESST workplace clearance certifying machine guarding, noise control, ventilation of vinyl plastisol vapors, and emergency evacuation procedures.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — Business Registration Online portal (www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/businesses.html). Provincial counterpart: Revenu Québec (www.revenuquebec.ca) for Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and provincial registration obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Quebec limited partnership (société en commandite) must obtain a federal Business Number (BN) from the CRA, including a GST/HST program account, by submitting Form RC148 or using Business Registration Online (BRO) with a 'partnership' registration. Registration is compulsory when taxable supplies exceed the $30,000 small-supplier threshold. Revenu Québec registration for QST must be completed separately via the Quebec business registration service (Inforoute/Données), requiring the BN, partnership contract, and authorized representative details. Non-resident partners triggering Canadian nexus must provide their foreign registration particulars and, if demanded, designate a Quebec agent for service.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box exists. The limited partnership's pass-through classification is non-elective for federal and Quebec income tax. Available elections include: (a) Income Tax Act s. 97(2) partnership rollover on contributed property; (b) s. 249.1(6) alternative fiscal-period election; (c) Excise Tax Act s. 156(2) election for nil consideration on qualifying intra-group supplies; and (d) hybrid mismatch rules in Income Tax Act ss. 12.7 and 18.6 which limit deduction/non-inclusion outcomes for partnership interests.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax) / QST (Quebec Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD $30,000 in GST/HST and QST taxable supplies over any single calendar quarter or the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (small-supplier threshold).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not impose real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory continuous controls, or digital stamping for invoices. Both CRA and Revenu Québec accept electronic invoicing and e-records, provided the invoice clearly states the supplier name and Business Number, the amount of GST/QST charged, and the nature of the supply. Taxpayers must retain all books and records in machine-readable form and provide audit access on request.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to exports of tangible personal property, including designer blind box toys, when the goods are exported by the supplier or by a non-resident purchaser through a common carrier within a reasonable time after delivery (Excise Tax Act, Schedule VI, Part V, s. 6). Quebec QST provides an equivalent zero-rating on exports (An Act respecting the Quebec Sales Tax, relevant exemption for goods exported outside Canada). The supplier must hold documentary evidence that the goods left Canada and that the purchaser is a non-resident. Services, such as design or finishing services supplied in connection with export-bound goods, may also be zero-rated if performed for a non-resident and the goods are subsequently exported.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A) or eManifest export record for commercial shipments; for low-value courier shipments, the courier's export manifest and shipment reference.
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or courier consignment note demonstrating physical departure of the goods from Canada and destination outside Canada.
Commercial invoice or sales contract identifying the non-resident purchaser and the international delivery terms (e.g., Incoterms), confirming title transfers only after export.
Proof of payment received from the non-resident buyer, including SWIFT/MT103, Star-Settle/Stripe/Shopify settlement records, or credit-card vouchers showing the foreign-currency remittance.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec closely scrutinize zero-rating substantiation. Deficient documentation leads to reassessment of unremitted GST/QST plus prescribed interest and a civil penalty of up to 25% of the net tax amount for false statements or gross negligence (Excise Tax Act s. 280; Taxation Act corresponding provisions). Retrospective assessments may extend to four years, or without time limit in cases of fraud or misrepresentation. Repeated or willful disregard can attract criminal prosecution. Although Canada imposes no statutory forex repatriation deadline, the 180-day benchmark is applied in audit practice; prolonged non-repatriation of export sales proceeds increases fraud-risk indicators and may negate zero-rating eligibility.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates under an IMF Article VIII regime providing full convertibility for current account transactions. Capital account transactions face no general restrictions for resident limited partnerships. Profit remittances to non-resident partners are permitted without prior approval, subject only to standard Income Tax Act withholding at source and automatic reporting via T5 slips. Quebec provincial entities benefit from the same federal convertibility framework with no additional capital controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion of export proceeds is required under Canadian law. Exporters may freely negotiate settlement terms with their banks. All export receipts must be recorded for Canada Revenue Agency tax compliance and may be reported through normal banking channels without prescribed conversion ratios or timelines.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility rating for cross-border e-commerce platforms including Shopify Payments and Stripe. Legal constraints include PCI DSS compliance, FINTRAC registration, and Quebec consumer protection requirements under the Consumer Protection Act. Offshore digital EMIs are permissible for eligible merchant categories provided robust AML/KYC controls and tax reporting obligations are maintained.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is permitted under revised Bank of Canada and FINTRAC guidelines with video KYC verification. Physical presence is required only for initial director interviews and beneficial owner verification in Quebec entities; subsequent transactions may proceed remotely.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of funds or beneficial ownership discrepancies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate registry extracts, partnership agreement, tax returns, source of wealth affidavits, and beneficial ownership declarations

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions involving high-risk jurisdictions or shell entities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank reference letters, trade references, and independent verification of business activity

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections utilize SWIFT MT103 or domestic wire transfers with purpose code 848 (Capital Contribution) or 840 (Equity Injection). All transactions require supporting documentation including the limited partnership agreement, board resolutions, and proof of tax residency. Verification follows FINTRAC guidelines and Quebec securities regulations where applicable.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements route through SWIFT MT103 for international wires, Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600, and correspondent banking networks. Purpose codes include 100 (Payment for Goods) or 200 (Service Fees). All disbursements undergo full AML screening and beneficiary verification prior to release.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual declaration update (déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the limited partnership's initial Quebec registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is subject to REQ administrative penalties; persistent failure to file for at least 24 months may lead to administrative strike-off of the enterprise's registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return for federal income allocation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the end of the partnership fiscal period; for a December 31 year-end, no later than May 31 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a CRA penalty of CAD 25 per day up to CAD 2,500; continued non-filing may result in additional penalties, partner-level reassessments, and enforcement measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec partnership information return (TP-600 counterpart) for provincial allocation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within six months after the end of the partnership fiscal period, matching the provincial filing requirement for a Quebec-based partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts provincial penalty and interest; repeated non-compliance may trigger liens or collection actions against partnership assets.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit is imposed on a Quebec limited partnership solely by law; an audit becomes mandatory only if required by the partnership agreement, lender covenants, securities regulatory status, or the audit obligations of a corporate general partner subject to Canadian securities legislation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements may be prepared under IFRS where the partnership is publicly accountable or under Canadian ASPE for private enterprises; tax reporting to CRA and Revenu Québec must use the accrual method and Canadian dollars.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec's legal-publicity regime does not create a separate UBO filing for limited partnerships; however, the annual declaration must confirm the names and addresses of all general partners and the principal place of business. Any change in general partners must be reported to REQ within 60 days of the change. Limited partners are not disclosed publicly unless they take part in control of the partnership.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Officers (where a corporate general partner is used)
Minute Book (partnership agreement, amendments, consents, capital contribution records)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000–10,000; incurred only where contractually or lender-required, not as a statutory annual condition

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
